transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because things at work have been… off. I drive routes, and dispatch and compliance keep tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there’ll be these little comments over the radio that sound like they’re about me. People say it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.

It’s hard to explain without sounding like I’m overthinking it. I mean, in transportation everybody watches everybody’s timing anyway, and there was this one time with a route change near the depot—sorry, I’m getting off track. It’s just been making me feel like I needed to talk to someone.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are deliberately monitoring and talking about you?

I mean… yes, I do think it’s on purpose. Dispatch and compliance can see when I change a route in the system, and then not long after there’ll be these little comments over the radio that line up too closely. People keep saying it’s just normal monitoring, but certain drivers are definitely reporting on me.

It’s like, I know how the job works—everyone’s timing gets watched, paperwork, route logs, all that—but this feels different. Like they’re paying attention to me specifically.
If someone offered clear proof that the radio comments were unrelated to you, would you still believe your coworkers were targeting you?

I mean… if it was really clear proof, I’d try to listen to that. But I don’t know, because it’s not just one comment. It’s the route changes showing up in the system, then dispatch or compliance knowing, and then certain drivers saying things that line up too much.

So… yeah, I think I’d still feel like something was going on. Maybe that one radio comment wasn’t about me, sure, but the whole pattern still feels like they’re watching me specifically. And at work people act like it’s all normal oversight, but I can tell when it’s more than that.
Have you ever heard voices when no one was actually there?

I don’t know… not like, clearly, I guess. Sometimes I think I hear something, but then it’s the radio or someone outside the bus, or the building settling—my apartment makes these weird noises at night, especially near the heater.

So I wouldn’t say I’ve heard voices with nobody there. I mean, I get confused about sounds sometimes, especially after a long shift, but I haven’t noticed like… a person talking to me when no one’s around.
Do you think it’s possible you might be mistaken about your coworkers targeting you?

I mean… I guess anything is possible, right? People tell me I’m reading into it. But it doesn’t feel like that from where I’m sitting.

Like, I change something in the route system, and then dispatch or compliance seems to know right away, and then there are these little comments over the radio. And I know computers track everything now—my phone updates without asking, my bank app does that thing where it freezes and then suddenly knows my location, which is annoying—but at work it’s different. Certain drivers just seem like they’re reporting on me.

So… maybe I could be mistaken about some part of it. But the whole thing? I don’t know. It feels too specific to just be normal oversight.
Aside from this issue at work, have you been having trouble managing your usual daily life?

Yeah… I mean, a little more than I want to admit, probably.

At work I’ve been falling behind on the route reports, and then when I do send instructions out, I guess they’re not always clear, because drivers have complained. Which is frustrating because I used to be pretty organized with that stuff. I had my own system with sticky notes and the color-coded folders—my husband always teased me about it because I’d label everything, even the junk drawer at home.

But lately at home, he’s been handling more things too. Like meals, phone calls, planning basic stuff. I’ll mean to do it and then it just… doesn’t happen, or I get mixed up and put it off. So yes, I’m keeping up with some things, but not like I used to.
Have other people told you that your speech or the way you explain things has become hard to follow?

Yeah… people have said that, kind of. Mostly at work. Like, drivers complain that my instructions don’t make sense or that they can’t tell what I want them to do, and then I have to go back through the route reports, which I’m already behind on.

It’s embarrassing, because I used to be really clear with that stuff. I’d have the routes laid out and notes and everything. My husband says I’ve been harder to pin down too, like when we’re talking about meals or making calls or planning something simple, I’ll start explaining and then somehow we’re talking about three other things. So he’s been taking over more of that. I don’t love admitting that.
Have you noticed yourself feeling emotionally flat or showing much less expression than usual?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I’m trying to be cold or anything. I just don’t seem to have the same… spark, I guess.

I used to sing with the choir, and I liked that, and we’d have the softball team over sometimes after games—nothing fancy, just snacks and people sitting around talking. Now even the idea of it feels like too much. Most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, like if I stare at it long enough dinner or phone calls or whatever will start itself.

And then suddenly it’s been an hour and I still haven’t done anything. So maybe I don’t show much, yeah. I feel kind of blank a lot.
About how long have you been experiencing this sense that your coworkers are specifically watching or reporting on you?

About two months, I think. That’s when it started feeling really clear to me, like the computer system was tracking what I was doing and the radio comments were… not just normal chatter, you know?

Before that, I don’t know, I might’ve brushed things off. Work is always noisy, and people talk, and the system logs everything anyway. But for the past couple months it’s felt more pointed, like it was about me.
Since these problems began, has there been a period of six months or longer when you were having these kinds of symptoms?

Yeah… I think it has been more than six months. It’s hard to put a clean line on it, because at first I thought it was just the new role, you know, being put as temporary dispatch lead and everybody needing something from me at once.

But if I count from then, it’s been about eight months. That’s when things started building up, and then it just sort of kept going.
